revenue_estimate.price_source: median of 1 prices with no stated period — treated as one-time, not recurring
revenue_estimate.note: MRR = observed price ($499.0 one-time) x assumed customers/mo (20 conservative, 200 optimistic). The customer counts are assumptions; the price is an observation.

negative_signals: 5 Product Hunt launches in this space

claude_analysis.tam_assessment: Niche research market: the 15 incumbents found are EEG hardware vendors (BrainBit, Mentalab, mBrainTrain, Bitbrain), not dedicated sync-tool sellers, and HN shows 0 results, so buyers are mostly university and neurotech labs running multi-device setups, with moderate and rising search interest (44.2 avg, up).
claude_analysis.pricing_assessment: The only observed price ($499, brainbit.com) is for hardware with no stated period, so standalone sync software likely sells for about $100/yr per lab, since vendors bundle sync into their SDKs and free open-source tools exist.
claude_analysis.legal_reasoning: The regulatory probe found no restriction terms and no government sources, and research-use timing software is not a regulated medical device claim.
key_risks: Free open-source standards such as Lab Streaming Layer (LSL) already handle multi-device EEG timestamp sync in research labs, which caps willingness to pay (from domain knowledge, not the research data)
Hardware vendors (BrainBit, Mentalab, mBrainTrain) bundle sync into their SDKs, so a third-party tool is hard to justify
Weak demand signal: 0 HN results, and the Reddit hits are mostly unrelated (e.g. CrackSupport)
key_opportunities: Search interest in EEG synchronization is rising (Google Trends up, avg 44.2)
Search results are not vendor-dominated (0% vendor share, 9/10 content pages), so organic/SEO entry is plausible
Labs mixing EEG with other devices (eye tracking, cameras, other brands) need cross-vendor sync that single-vendor SDKs don't provide
claude_analysis.value_reasoning: About 10,000 potential labs × about $100/yr per customer ≈ $1M total addressable annual revenue.
claude_analysis.probability_reasoning: Crowded competition caps this at 0.10, and a free, widely used open-source standard plus sync bundled into vendor SDKs push realistic paid penetration below 1% of an already niche market.
